requirement: Implement TimeoutHTTPAdapter and create_timeout_session enforcing default connect and read timeouts on all requests. It must validate that timeouts are strictly positive, replace timeout=None with default_timeout in send(), preserve caller-specified positive timeouts, and mount the adapter to both http:// and https:// schemes.
skeleton: TimeoutHTTPAdapter subclass of HTTPAdapter and create_timeout_session factory enforcing non-null timeouts.

rationale.teaches: An HTTPAdapter subclass that enforces a (connect, read) default timeout, validates positivity, respects a caller's explicit positive timeout, and is mounted on both schemes.
rationale.why: requests has no default timeout, so an unmodified adapter hangs forever on a silent peer. The fixture intercepts send and reads the effective timeout, since a real hang cannot be tested.

candidates.why_wrong: The default timeout is a single 60 second value, so connect and read share one budget instead of the separate 3.05 and 27 seconds.
Zero and negative timeouts are accepted, so a caller can disable the timeout by passing 0.
The check uses <, so a timeout of exactly 0 is accepted.
The caller's timeout is always overridden with the default, so a request that needs a longer read timeout cannot get one.
A plain HTTPAdapter is mounted instead of TimeoutHTTPAdapter, so no default timeout is ever applied.
